title: Nearly Half of Regular U.S. AI Users Say They Have Bent the Truth to Get Past AI Customer Service, New TELUS Digital Poll Finds
summary: Poll of 1,000 regular U.S. AI users: nearly half said they bent the truth to reach a person, and 89% said they used a workaround when AI fell short.
body_markdown:
**Vancouver, B.C. (November 17, 2026)** -[TELUS Digital](https://www.telusdigital.com/) , a global technology service provider specializing in AI-powered digital customer experiences (CX) and future-focused digital transformations, today released results of a new poll finding that nearly half of regular U.S. AI users (46%) said they have bent the truth by giving exaggerated or not entirely accurate information to get past an automated customer service system and reach a person. 89% said they have used a workaround when AI did not understand or resolve their issue, such as rewording their question or asking for a human agent.


TELUS Digital’s poll of 1,000 U.S. adults who regularly use AI found that 57% chose an AI-powered tool when reaching out for customer service because they expected it to be the fastest option, but about three in ten respondents (30%) said they have dropped a purchase after finding that AI was the main way to get customer service. More than three-quarters of respondents (77%) said a guaranteed human support option would make them more likely to choose one company over another for everyday purchases, suggesting that access to a person may help enterprises win and keep customers.


“Nearly half of the people we polled said they’ve bent the truth to get past an automated system, and most said they have used other workarounds, which suggests gaps in how some customer experiences are built,” said Jamie Timm, Global SVP of Service Delivery and Operations at TELUS Digital. “Those gaps matter as we see that revenue may be at stake. Some respondents said they have walked away from a purchase when AI was the main way to get help, and most said guaranteed access to a person would make them more likely to choose one company over another. Keeping customers and relieving frustration calls for AI that understands their requests and resolves their issues, alongside human agents who are easy to reach and have real-time guidance and context when a customer needs a person. TELUS Digital helps enterprises bring the two together as a cohesive omnichannel experience, with the consulting, engineering and operations to run it.”


#### **What frustrates people most about AI customer service?**


Respondents were asked to choose the one part of dealing with AI-powered customer service that was most burdensome to them from a list of eight options. Three answers accounted for 60% of responses:


- Explaining the problem in a way the AI understands (23%)


- Repeating the same information (22%)


- Difficulty reaching a human, or no option to reach one (15%)


The first two relate to how well AI interpreted a request and kept track of what a customer had already shared, while the third relates to how easily customers could reach a person when they needed one. The other five options, each chosen by 10% of respondents or fewer, were inaccurate or contradictory answers (10%), waiting for the AI to respond (9%), navigating menus or irrelevant response options (9%), not knowing whether the AI can resolve the issue (8%) and spending more time than the problem is worth (4%).


#### **How do customers work around AI customer service?**


Respondents indicated they rarely stopped trying when AI customer service fell short, with only 12% saying they gave up on their issue. Most said they have tried something else to get the help they needed (respondents could select more than one):


- 47% simplified or rewrote their explanation


- 42% asked the same question a different way


- 35% asked for a human agent


- 28% restarted the chat or opened a new session


- 26% repeated the same request several times


In a separate question, respondents were asked whether they had ever given exaggerated or not entirely accurate information to get past an automated customer service system and reach a person. Nearly half (46%) said they have, including a third (33%) who said they have done it more than once. The behavior was more common among younger respondents, with 57% of those ages 18 to 29 saying they had, compared with 32% of those ages 62 to 75.


#### **What does it cost enterprises when AI customer service falls short?**


Respondents’ answers pointed to risk to customer engagement, trust and sales for enterprises:


- More than half (56%) said they avoid AI customer service at least half of the time when another option is available


- 30% said they have abandoned a purchase after seeing that AI was the primary customer service option


- If they had to use a workaround, 26% said they would give feedback or file a complaint, and 17% said they would lose trust in the company’s ability to address their needs


#### **How can enterprises close the AI customer service gap?**


TELUS Digital offers enterprises end-to-end AI-powered CX solutions that combine consulting, engineering and the teams to run them. Through[digital CX transformation](https://www.telusdigital.com/solutions/cx-consulting) solutions, TELUS Digital helps enterprises identify where AI fits in the customer journey. Through[customer care AI & technology](https://www.telusdigital.com/solutions/ai-customer-care) , its[conversational AI solutions](https://www.telusdigital.com/solutions/ai-customer-care/intelligent-conversational-ai-solutions) combine voice, generative AI and agentic automation so AI agents can handle routine requests across channels and languages and pass the conversation to a human agent, with context, when an interaction needs a person.


To support human agents, TELUS Digital’s[AI-powered agent tools](https://www.telusdigital.com/solutions/ai-customer-care/ai-powered-agent-tools) offer real-time guidance during live conversations, analyze interactions to support quality and coaching, and use AI-generated simulations to help new agents practice before taking live calls. TELUS Digital connects these solutions to enterprises’ contact center platforms, CRM systems and backend systems, and its customer service and[contact center management](https://www.telusdigital.com/solutions/contact-center-outsourcing/contact-center-management) teams run and optimize the blend of AI and human support, backed by 80,000+ team members across 35+ countries.


“Customers shouldn’t have to use a workaround to get help,” added Timm. “In our CX operations, we sort customer interactions into four types, and each calls for a different strategy: simple tasks customers can handle themselves through self-service, routine requests that automation can resolve, complex issues where a person steps in supported by AI, and proactive outreach, where the company contacts the customer first, based on their circumstances and preferences, before they need to ask. With enterprises, we look at the interactions their customers have and build an AI strategy designed to support each type.”


To learn more about TELUS Digital’s end-to-end AI-powered CX solutions, visit[telusdigital.com](http://telusdigital.com/)


**Poll Methodology:** *TELUS Digital’s findings are based on a Pollfish questionnaire conducted in September 2026 with 1,000 adults aged 18 - 75 who live in the United States and who use AI assistants (such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude). The poll was conducted online and in the U.S.; results are self-reported and may not be representative of all regular AI users. Questions covered customer service interactions across industries including retail, travel, financial services and healthcare.*
